vscode.derive-files.apply-adopt-and-ejec: Apply, Adopt and Eject are in the context menu of the file in the Health view.
vscode.derive-files.derived-files-what-s: Derived files: what smith derive would write
vscode.derive-files.smith-writes-every-d: smith writes every derived file that is stale or missing and records it in smith.lock. It leaves the files someone edited alone.
vscode.derive-files.smith-overwrites-the: smith overwrites the file with the derived content. Your edit is lost; git can bring it back.
vscode.derive-files.smith-keeps-your-edi: smith keeps your edit as the new baseline. This works for a file smith owns by keys that still has every derived key. If the inputs change later, the file is in drift again.
vscode.derive-files.the-file-becomes-you: The file becomes yours. smith writes "you" as its owner in smith.lock and never touches it again.
vscode.derive-files.by-default-smith-lea:
{effect}

By default smith leaves the files uncommitted: review them with git. The commit button makes it one commit that Undo can revert.
vscode.derive-files.monosmith-commit-it-: MonoSmith: {part} {part2}. Commit it together with smith.lock.
vscode.derive-files.monosmith-choose-a-d: MonoSmith: choose a derived file first. Right-click it in the Health view, or open it in the editor and run the command again.
vscode.derive-files.monosmith-smith-has-: MonoSmith: smith has nothing to write for {file}. Refresh the Health view to read the derived files again.
vscode.derive-files.the-inputs-changed-a: The inputs changed and nobody edited the file. Apply rewrites it.
vscode.derive-files.the-file-is-gone-app: The file is gone. Apply writes it back.
vscode.derive-files.the-file-is-right-bu: The file is right but smith.lock does not list it. Apply records it.
vscode.derive-files.someone-edited-the-f: Someone edited the file. Explain shows the diff. Then Apply overwrites it, Adopt keeps the edit, or Eject makes the file yours.
vscode.derive-files.the-file-differs-fro: The file differs from what the sibling projects share. Explain shows the diff. Then Apply follows the siblings, or Eject keeps the file as yours.
vscode.derive-files.smith-cannot-edit-th: smith cannot edit the file (a region without its markers, or a file that does not parse). Fix the file, or Eject it.
